therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade and CTLA-4 immune checkpoint blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: T-cell activation and anti-tumor immune response
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Recurrent or Metastatic PD-L1-positive or -Negative Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck

results.effect_size: Durvalumab + Tremelimumab vs SoC: HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.85-1.26; Durvalumab vs SoC: HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72-1.08
biomarker_changes: PD-L1 positive patients had worse outcomes with combination therapy (median OS 4.8 months) compared to monotherapy (9.8 months) or standard of care (9.0 months)
subgroup_findings: PD-L1 negative patients showed similar outcomes across all arms
Duration of response was longer with immunotherapy (7.4-12.9 months) vs standard of care (3.7 months)
